SVREPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Western Hudspeth County in western Texas...
East central El Paso County in western Texas...

* Until 1100 PM MDT.

* At 1036 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 7 miles east of
Horizon City, moving northeast at 25 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage
to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Desert Haven, Lake Way Estates, and Hueco Mountain Wind Ranch.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Coastal flooding, with water levels of 1 to 2.5 feet
above the normal highest tide line, and 30 to 40 mph southwest
winds with gusts up to 40 to 55 mph.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, including Kipnuk, Kwigillingok
and Kongiganak.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM AKDT Wednesday, highest water levels expected
during each upcoming high tide through Wednesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Coastal flooding of low lying areas and erosion are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Steady south to southwesterly flow is
expected to continue for the Kuskokwim Delta coastline through
Wednesday morning as a series of low pressure systems track
across the Bering Sea. Coastal erosion and minor coastal
flooding will be possible with each upcoming high tide due to
the persistent onshore winds, during which maximum water levels
will reach between 1 and 2.5 ft above the normal highest tide
line, including in and around Kipnuk and Kwigillingok. The
strong winds may reduce the ability for flood waters to recede
during and close to low tide, possibly leading to prolonged
higher than normal water levels along the coast and near the
mouth of the Kuskokwim River. There will be a break in strong
winds between Wednesday afternoon and Thursday morning,
however, we are monitoring the potential for another strong
storm system that could cause additional coastal impacts towards
the end of this week.

events.region: Northeast Highlands; Eastern San Miguel County; Guadalupe County; Roosevelt County; De Baca County; Chaves County Plains
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of east central, northeast, and southeast New
Mexico, including the following areas, in east central New Mexico,
De Baca County, Guadalupe County and Roosevelt County. In northeast
New Mexico, Eastern San Miguel County and Northeast Highlands. In
southeast New Mexico, Chaves County Plains.

* WHEN...Until 6 AM MDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Showers and thunderstorms will continue overnight. With
additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches and localized
amounts of 2 to 3 inches, areas that were recently impacted by
heavy rainfall will be especially susceptible to additional flash
flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/abq/EmergencyPrepFlood

FFWEPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
East Central El Paso County in western Texas...

* Until 115 AM MDT.

* At 1009 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 1.5 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
East El Paso, Far East El Paso, Mission Valley, Horizon City,
Socorro, Sparks and Butterfield.
